name: Godfrey Phillips India Ltd
tagline: Rs 32,962 Cr cigarette maker outgrowing ITC/VST on domestic volumes through 2024, but posting a sharp Q1 FY27 revenue decline more recently
business_overview: Godfrey Phillips is India's second-largest cigarette manufacturer (Marlboro under license from Philip Morris, plus domestic brands), long viewed by the community as an undervalued, professionally-improving business relative to peers ITC and VST Industries.
fundamentals_narrative: Strong trailing profile (ROE 21.56%, near debt-free, 5-year revenue CAGR of ~21%), but the most recent data point is concerning: Q1 FY27 revenue (excl. excise duty) declined 19.2% YoY to Rs 1,191.85 Cr from Rs 1,474.25 Cr in Q1 FY26 — a sharp reversal from the multi-year outperformance the community had been tracking through 2024. Re-verified 2026-08-22: sharp one-year market-cap decline (-43%) confirmed, consistent with the tax-driven revenue headwinds noted in the thread; ROCE (13.4%) is more modest than the ROE headline suggests.
technical_read: Not pulled this pass — no browser escalation triggered.

trusted_signals.note: Detailed FY24Q2 volume-growth comparison showing Godfrey outperforming ITC and VST on domestic cigarette volumes, with Marlboro +27%. Portfolio thread separately named it a partial-sell-still-held / 'working right now' position.

bull_case: Multi-quarter track record (through early 2024) of outgrowing larger peers ITC and VST on domestic cigarette volumes, with a strong Marlboro relaunch story
Clean balance sheet (almost debt-free) with solid ROE (21.56%)
Trusted-user diligence (harsh.beria93) corroborates the historical outperformance with specific, sourced data rather than a vague endorsement
bear_case: Q1 FY27 revenue declined a sharp 19.2% YoY — a meaningful and recent reversal that the community thread (last substantively updated in 2024) has not yet processed or explained
At Rs 32,962 Cr market cap, this is a large-cap; even sustained strong growth would not mathematically deliver a 10x-in-2-3-years or realistic 100x-in-10-years outcome
Cigarette/tobacco sector carries structural regulatory and taxation overhang risk common to the category
verdict_headline: Well-run large-cap tobacco name with a genuine trusted-user growth thesis through 2024 — but a sharp, more recent revenue decline and its sheer size both argue against a multibagger case
verdict_reasoning: harsh.beria93's (trusted) detailed volume-growth comparison is a real, well-sourced conviction signal, but it is now roughly two years old and predates a sharp Q1 FY27 revenue decline (-19.2% YoY) that the ValuePickr thread has not yet caught up to or explained — this is exactly the kind of recent-quarter shift the methodology guidance warns against ignoring, except here it cuts against the bull case rather than for it.

At Rs 32,962 Cr market cap, Godfrey Phillips is unambiguously too large for a 10x-in-2-3-years case, and even a 100x-in-10-years outcome is not credible for a mature, regulation-exposed cigarette business of this size.

No solvency, promoter, or regulatory red flag was found — the revenue decline is a business-performance concern, not a red-flag-tier issue — so per the conviction floor for very-high trusted candidates, conviction is still set to Medium-High.
Worth a lighter follow-up specifically to understand the Q1 FY27 revenue drop before treating the earlier trusted thesis as still current.

Re-verification pass (2026-08-22): source (harsh.beria93) is elevated-tier, not top-tier — no automatic floor. Conviction corrected down from Medium-High to Low-Medium: the trusted peer-comparison notes are dated to Feb 2024, well before the sharp Q1 FY27 revenue decline and the stock's subsequent ~43% one-year fall — the underlying signal is stale relative to current conditions.
